title: Multikingdom gut microbiome machine learning distinguishes multiple sclerosis patients
summary: Fecal metagenomes (discovery cohort n = 1152; 1306 across 3 cohorts) were used to train sex-specific machine-learning models combining bacterial, fungal, viral and functional features. Cross-validated AUCs were 0.977 for males and 0.978 for females, but on external validation the ensemble models reached 0.813 and 0.745 and the 30-marker models 0.849 and 0.763.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifiers on multikingdom taxonomic and functional gut metagenome features

evidence.tested: External validation datasets: ensemble AUC 0.813 (males) and 0.745 (females); 30-marker models 0.849 and 0.763.
evidence.unknown: Modest external performance; case-control association, not causation; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning built the classifiers that distinguish MS patients from healthy controls.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
